name: Jared Galloway
summary: Bioinformatician and ML scientist with nine years of experience building research software for sequencing data. Builds Nextflow or Snakemake workflows on HPC clusters and AWS, including viral genomic surveillance. Develops models in PyTorch and JAX, from transformers to sparse statistical models. Co-author of more than 20 publications with 1,800+ citations.
bio: I build bioinformatics pipelines, machine learning models, and the software that puts them to work on noisy, high-dimensional sequencing data. I hold a B.S. in Computer & Information Science and an M.S. in Biology. Over nine years, I have developed methods in research groups at HHMI, Fred Hutch, and the University of Oregon.

I work across the whole analysis lifecycle, from raw sequencing data to published results. That means building reproducible workflows in Nextflow or Snakemake, fitting models in PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow, then validating them on simulated and experimental data. The resulting open-source packages run at scale on HPC clusters and AWS.

That work has contributed to more than 20 publications with 1,800+ citations, in journals including *Cell*, *eLife*, and *Bioinformatics*. Most recently, I built transformer models of natural selection in viral proteins.

I left the Matsen Lab in August 2026 and am looking for my next role in bioinformatics or applied machine learning. I take pride in clearly communicating my work and enjoy the discussions that follow.
